walkthrough:
Calculate the total distance $s$ moved up the slope:
$$s = v \times t = 1.8 \times 15 = 27\text{ m}$$

Calculate the vertical height gained $h$:
$$h = s\sin 20^\circ = 27\sin 20^\circ \approx 27(0.342020) = 9.2345\text{ m}$$

Calculate the change in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta PE = mgh = 5(10)(9.2345) \approx 462\text{ J}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work\u2013Energy Principle: Computes distance $27\text{ m}$ and finds $\Delta PE = 5(10)(27)\sin 20^\circ \approx 462\text{ J}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Find the distance travelled by the box along the line of greatest slope:
At constant speed $v = 1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for duration $t = 15\text{ s}$:
$$s = v \times t = 1.8 \times 15 = 27\text{ m}$$

Determine the vertical height gained:
Since the plane is inclined at $20^\circ$ to the horizontal:
$$h = s\sin 20^\circ = 27\sin 20^\circ\text{ m}$$

Calculate the change in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta PE = mgh$$
Substitute $m = 5\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h = 27\sin 20^\circ$:
$$\Delta PE = 5(10)(27\sin 20^\circ) = 1350\sin 20^\circ$$
Evaluate $\sin 20^\circ \approx 0.342020$:
$$\Delta PE = 1350 \times 0.342020 = 461.727\text{ J}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\Delta PE = 462\text{ J}$.

hints: At constant speed, kinetic energy does not change, so the work done by the pulling force equals the PE gain plus the work done against friction.
Calculate the work done against the $40\text{ N}$ frictional force over $27\text{ m}$: $W_f = 40 \times 27 = 1080\text{ J}$.
Add the potential energy gain from part (a): $W_{\text{pull}} = 461.73 + 1080$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the work done against friction over distance $s = 27\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = F_{\text{friction}} \times s = 40 \times 27 = 1080\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy balance with constant speed (no change in kinetic energy):
$$W_{\text{pull}} = \Delta PE + W_{\text{friction}}$$
$$W_{\text{pull}} = 461.73 + 1080 = 1541.73\text{ J} \approx 1540\text{ J}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work\u2013Energy Principle: Calculates work against friction $1080\text{ J}$ and adds PE gain to obtain total work $1540\text{ J}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy balance for steady motion up the inclined plane:
Because the box travels at constant speed, $\Delta KE = 0$.
By the work-energy theorem:
$$W_{\text{pull}} - W_{\text{friction}} = \Delta PE$$
$$W_{\text{pull}} = \Delta PE + W_{\text{friction}}$$

Calculate the work done against the opposing frictional force:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = F_{\text{friction}} \times s$$
Substitute $F_{\text{friction}} = 40\text{ N}$ and distance $s = 27\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = 40 \times 27 = 1080\text{ J}$$

Sum the two energy requirements:
$$W_{\text{pull}} = 461.727 + 1080 = 1541.727\text{ J}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $1540\text{ J}$.
Alternatively, compute the pulling force directly:
$$F_{\text{pull}} = mg\sin 20^\circ + 40 = 50\sin 20^\circ + 40 \approx 17.101 + 40 = 57.101\text{ N}$$
$$W_{\text{pull}} = F_{\text{pull}} \times s = 57.101 \times 27 \approx 1541.7\text{ J} \approx 1540\text{ J}$$.
